note: Hand-authored. `quote` is verbatim from https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9207 with line wrapping removed and nothing else changed.

requirements.quote: In authorization responses to the client, including error responses, an authorization server supporting this specification MUST indicate its identity by including the iss parameter in the response.
requirements.applies: apps/auth-server/src/app/helpers/oauth-redirect.ts (buildRedirectUrl) — every /oauth/authorize redirect, success and error alike.
requirements.evidenceMatch: on every authorization response|on the success response

requirements.quote: The iss parameter value is the issuer identifier of the authorization server that created the authorization response, as defined in [RFC8414]. Its value MUST be a URL that uses the "https" scheme without any query or fragment components.
requirements.applies: apps/auth-server/src/app/helpers/discovery.ts (resolveIssuerIdentifier) — the single function that produces both the emitted iss and the advertised issuer.

requirements.quote: The issuer identifier included in the server's metadata value issuer MUST be identical to the iss parameter's value.
requirements.applies: apps/auth-server/src/app/helpers/discovery.ts — resolveIssuerIdentifier feeds both the metadata `issuer` member and the authorization-response `iss`, so the two cannot drift.

requirements.quote: The server MUST indicate its support for the iss parameter by setting the metadata parameter authorization_response_iss_parameter_supported, defined in Section 3, to true.
requirements.applies: apps/auth-server/src/app/helpers/discovery.ts — hard-coded true on both the RFC 8414 and the OIDC documents, matching the unconditional emission.

requirements.quote: Clients that support this specification MUST extract the value of the iss parameter from authorization responses they receive if the parameter is present.
requirements.reason: A relying-party obligation. QAuth is the authorization server; nothing in this repository consumes an authorization response, so the requirement never applies to it.

requirements.quote: authorization_response_iss_parameter_supported: Boolean parameter indicating whether the authorization server provides the iss parameter in the authorization response as defined in Section 2. If omitted, the default value is false.
